subject: ss-neurology
title: Higher Cortical Functions, Aphasia and Apraxia

steps.tx: **Broca aphasia** (expressive, motor aphasia) localizes to the posterior inferior frontal gyrus (**Brodmann** areas 44 and 45), producing non-fluent, effortful, agrammatic speech with intact auditory comprehension but impaired repetition. Patients exhibit prominent frustration and awareness of language deficits due to intact self-monitoring capabilities.
steps.say: Broca aphasia results from damage involving the posterior inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant cerebral hemisphere. Spoken language is non fluent, sparse, effortful, and telegraphic with omitted grammatical words. Auditory language comprehension remains relatively intact, whereas verbal repetition is significantly impaired.

steps.tx: **Wernicke aphasia** (receptive, sensory aphasia) localizes to the posterior superior **temporal gyrus** (Brodmann area 22), presenting with fluent, paraphasic speech, profound comprehension loss, and severely impaired repetition. Patients exhibit prominent anosognosia, completely unaware of their severe conversational communication breakdown and neologistic errors.
steps.say: Wernicke aphasia arises from lesions situated in the posterior superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere. Patients produce fluent, melodic speech that is riddled with neologisms and paraphasic errors, rendering output completely incomprehensible. Both auditory comprehension and verbal repetition are profoundly defective, and patients typically demonstrate complete lack of awareness of their deficit.

steps.tx: Disconnection between anterior and posterior language centers produces isolated repetition failure. **Conduction aphasia** is caused by lesions damaging the **arcuate fasciculus** or supramarginal gyrus. Patients demonstrate normal fluency and preserved auditory language comprehension, but exhibit disproportionately severe impairment in verbal **repetition** with prominent phonemic paraphasias. Patients repeatedly attempt to self-correct their pronunciation errors, termed conduit d'approche.
steps.say: Conduction aphasia is a classic disconnection syndrome caused by lesions disrupting the arcuate fasciculus within the dominant hemisphere. Spontaneous conversational speech is fluent and auditory language comprehension is preserved. However, patients have severe impairment in repetition alongside prominent phonemic paraphasias and recurrent attempts at self correction.

steps.tx: **Klüver-Bucy syndrome** results from bilateral anterior temporal lobe damage involving the **amygdalae**, producing hyperorality, hypersexuality, psychic blindness (visual agnosia), docility, and dietary alterations. This contrasts with global aphasia, which damages the entire dominant middle cerebral artery perisylvian language territory, obliterating all language modalities.
steps.say: Klüver Bucy syndrome arises from bilateral anterior temporal lobe destruction involving the amygdalae. Patients exhibit psychic blindness, hyperorality, hypersexuality, and marked emotional docility.

steps.tx: Parietal association cortex damage generates distinctive neuropsychological syndromes. **Gerstmann syndrome** is a classic tetrad localizing to the **angular gyrus** of the dominant parietal lobe. It consists of **finger agnosia** (inability to identify fingers), right-left disorientation, **agraphia** (inability to write), and **acalculia** (inability to perform mathematical calculations), occurring in the absence of generalized dementia.
steps.say: Gerstmann syndrome localizes to the angular gyrus of the dominant parietal lobe. It is characterized clinically by a tetrad of findings: finger agnosia, right left disorientation, agraphia, and acalculia. Recognizing this distinct symptom cluster allows precise anatomical localization to the dominant inferior parietal lobule.

steps.tx: **Hemispatial neglect** syndrome (inattention) characteristically occurs following acute destructive lesions of the non-dominant right **inferior parietal lobule** or temporoparietal junction. Patients fail to respond or orient to stimuli presented in the left hemispace, frequently exhibiting anosognosia and asomatognosia regarding their paralyzed limbs.
steps.say: Lesions involving the non dominant right parietal lobe impair spatial attention and body schema perception. Affected individuals exhibit contralateral spatial hemineglect, ignoring visual, auditory, and tactile stimuli in the left hemispace. Patients frequently display anosognosia, vehemently denying their dense left hemiplegia or disowning their paralyzed limbs.

steps.tx: **Balint syndrome** localizes to bilateral parieto-occipital cortical lesions, producing the clinical triad of optic ataxia (inability to reach visually guided targets), ocular apraxia (inability to direct voluntary saccades), and **simultanagnosia** (inability to perceive more than one visual item at once).
steps.say: Bálint syndrome is caused by bilateral parieto occipital border zone lesions. It consists of a triad comprising simultanagnosia, optic ataxia, and ocular apraxia. Patients have normal visual acuity but cannot perceive more than one object simultaneously, failing to comprehend complex visual scenes.

steps.tx: **Anton syndrome** (**visual anosognosia**) occurs with extensive bilateral striate occipital cortex infarction, where patients are cortically blind yet adamantly deny blindness and confabulate visual experiences. Ideomotor apraxia represents a separate disorder of learned motor planning caused by left parietal lesions.
steps.say: Anton syndrome represents visual anosognosia caused by bilateral occipital lobe infarction. Cortically blind individuals adamantly deny their loss of vision and confabulate detailed visual descriptions of their surroundings.
